newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel - EMU prospects unchanged by 97 tax shortfall.
newsitem.headline: Waigel - EMU prospects unchanged by 97 tax shortfall.

text.p: German finance minister Theo Waigel said on Thursday that an estimated 18 billion mark ($10.6 billion) shortfall in German tax revenues in 1997 did not alter the country's chances of meeting European single currency requirements.
"(The estimated shortfall) does not lead to a fundamentally different appraisal in relation to the Maastricht criteria (for monetary union)," Waigel said in a statement.
Waigel said the shortfall "was in large part not a result of current economic developments but of (the level of) tax payments and refunds from previous years".

He noted however that the tax position had been hit by continuing weak employment levels and the fact that economic growth was being largely led by exports, which did not bring in as much tax revenue as purely domestic growth.
Waigel added that the tax shortfalls foreseen between 1998 and 2001 were yet another argument for a "far-reaching tax reform", as currently being planned by the government.
